sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Bulk Export of Organic Dried Lycium and Herbal Botanicals

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (commercial and foundation law derived from the Panamanian Civil Code, supplemented by modern private foundation and trust statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Double Taxation Agreements with Mexico, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg
Tax Information Exchange Agreements with the United States and the United Kingdom

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Special Regime of Private Interest Foundations) as amended; Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT and its implementing Cabinet Decree No. 710 of 27 April 2015, as updated by subsequent Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) resolutions; beneficial ownership data must be filed with the Public Registry and maintained by the registered agent, available to Panamanian competent authorities in compliance with OECD Global Forum transparency requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (executed before registration at the Public Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama only if the charter must be presented abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted by the Founder to the registered agent for formation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the Founder's country of origin or a Panamanian Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague-member states) OR Consular Legalization by the Panamanian Embassy (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Founder's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National immigration or passport authority of the country of origin plus notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter covering the initial minimum foundation capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the Founder maintains the account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence for any corporate founder or corporate Foundation Council member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record or police clearance certificate for the Foundation Council members and the Protector (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of the Founder, Foundation Council members, Protector, designated beneficiaries and any contributor of foundation capital against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, and Panama's own UAF/FIU sanction and administrative databases. Any PEP, PEP family member or close associate triggers enhanced due diligence with documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence before the Foundation Charter is notarized.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) - Electronic services portal (eRegistro / Portal de Servicios en Línea del Registro Público), Department of Corporate Registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Foundation Charter must be written in Spanish. A foundation name in a foreign language requires a Spanish transliteration recorded in the charter; the name must end with the word 'Fundación' or the expression 'Fundación de Interés Privado' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing company, foundation or trademark recorded in the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name availability certificate (Certificado de Búsqueda) is valid for 30 calendar days. A single renewal may be requested if registration is imminent. Upon rejection, counsel files a written reconsideration request with the Director General of the Public Registry within 5 business days of the rejection ruling; a further hierarchical appeal may be lodged. Final recourse is judicial review before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice. To avoid delay, parallel submission under a materially modified name is recommended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual address is not permissible as the statutory registered office: Law No. 25 of 1995 requires a licensed Panamanian lawyer (registered agent) to maintain a physical office in Panama where the foundation charter, book of resolutions, records and visitor log are kept. A virtual office may be used only for commercial correspondence and logistics abroad and does not satisfy the registered-office or economic-substance test.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the 'Low_Risk_Standard' dried-herb wholesale tier: approximately 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the UAF/FIU or the registered agent's internal compliance team under current risk-based supervision. The probability escalates to 20-30% if UBO records are incomplete, registered-agent cooperation is not maintained, or high-risk correspondent payment flows are detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 2013, Ley No. 8 de 2022, and Ley No. 70 de 2023; Article 7 (registration requirement), Article 10 (foundation charter contents), Article 21 (resident agent), and Article 26 (foundation council).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Dirección General de Registro, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, located in Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Fundacional (Foundation Charter), duly notarized, together with the Reglamento (Foundation Rules), inscribed in the Register of Private Interest Foundations; the registry subsequently issues the Certificado de Personería Jurídica (Certificate of Legal Existence/Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Law 25 of 1995, but the Founder must irrevocably allocate an initial endowment (patrimonio fundacional) to the foundation's purposes; for this international trading entity, a nominal endowment of at least USD 10,000 is industry-standard to evidence substance. No escrow account is required under Panamanian law; escrow arrangements, if any, arise only as a condition of commercial bank onboarding.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL, UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION [NAME], ADOPTED IN LIEU OF AN IN-PERSON FIRST MEETING. RESOLVED: (1) the initial endowment contributed by the Founder is accepted and shall be administered exclusively for the international wholesale trading of organic dried goji berries (Lycium barbarum), herbal botanicals, and related products; (2) the registered office is fixed at the office of the Resident Agent, [AGENT], at [ADDRESS], Panama City, Republic of Panama; (3) [COUNCIL MEMBERS] are appointed as Foundation Council members, with [NAME] as President, and [PROTECTOR] as Protector; (4) the Council and authorized signatories are empowered to open bank accounts, sign SWIFT/wire instructions, and execute export documentation. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Foundation Charter and Rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of Panama (Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Acta Fundacional and Reglamento in Spanish. The Founder, or an attorney-in-fact under a special power of attorney, must appear before a Panamanian notary to execute the charter, declare the initial endowment, and approve the foundation rules. Verify that the resident agent is identified and the registered office coincides with the resident agent's address. If foreign execution is contemplated, obtain apostille and authenticated notarial copy.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Founder's passport or ID
Notarized special power of attorney (if signing by proxy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or attorney identifies formal defects, issue a corrective notarial addendum (addendum protocol) before submission; any material amendment requires a new Founder's resolution and re-execution of the charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of stamp taxes and filing of the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official registry and stamp tax fees (timbre fiscal) at an authorized banking entity or via relevant government collection platform. Submit the executed foundation charter, known as 'inscripción', with three notarial copies, payment receipts, and the resident agent's appointment. The registry assigns a folio real number and reviews formal legality of the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry fee and stamp tax
Certificate of payment of the Public Registry annualized fee, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a 'razón de no inscripción' (refusal notice), the attorney must file a formal correction or an amendment deed within the statutory term, addressing the specific legal objections raised, and resubmit for inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Legal Existence and Foundation Folio
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección General de Registro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription is perfected, request the certified Certificate of Legal Existence (Certificado de Personería Jurídica) and a certified printout of the foundation folio. Confirm the foundation name, date of acquisition of legal personality, and registered office details. Obtain an authenticated Spanish-language certificate and, where required for foreign banking, an English courtesy translation.
required_dossiers: Notarial copy of the inscribed charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or contains errors, file a written request for rectification or expedited issuance with supporting notarial evidence; registry correction notices can be processed by the delegated attorney without new filing fees beyond the official tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Resident Agent record, tax registration and annual obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the resident agent and registered office continuously. Register the foundation with DGI to obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). File the statutory annual fee of USD 300 (tasa anual de fundación) within the relevant period. Complete and file annual economic substance reporting demonstrating that no relevant activity is carried out in Panama, and that the foundation's income is foreign-source and therefore outside Panamanian territorial taxation.
required_dossiers: Resident agent acceptance and registered office declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of late filing penalties for the annual fee or economic substance return, submit a waiving brief with supporting evidence of force majeure or bona fide error through the resident agent; DGI and the Registry accept administrative settlements for first-time compliance failures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and payment rail activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supervising authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá; execution: licensed commercial bank in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate current account in the name of the Private Interest Foundation at a licensed Panamanian bank. Submit the full formation dossier to the bank's compliance department for AML/KYC review under Custodian Law 23 of 2015. Provide the beneficial ownership declaration, endowment source-of-funds evidence, and the first council resolution authorizing signatories. Confirm activation of SWIFT TT and wire transfer routes; the bank may impose minimum deposit conditions.
required_dossiers: Register of Beneficial Owners (current sworn form)
Founder and Council members' passport copies
Bank application forms and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires Enhanced Due Diligence, provide a notarized source-of-funds affidavit, audited commercial background, and trade references (sales contract preliminaries); if rejected, resubmit to an alternative licensed bank with the same complete or reinforced dossier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Industrias, jointly with Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), Dirección General de Salud, Departamento de Alimentos y Bebidas.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento para Alimentos y Bebidas (MINSA sanitary operating permit) and Certificado de Libre Venta (Certificate of Free Sale) for export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals; plus, where a conditioning or packaging warehouse is established, the Licencia Industrial de Funcionamiento (MICI industrial operating license).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Seguimiento y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Declaración Jurada de Impacto Ambiental (environmental affidavit) for low-impact dry botanical warehousing, sorting and repackaging. A full Environmental and Social Impact Study (Category III) is not required; upgrade to Category II assessment applies only if mechanized drying, grinding/extraction lines or other significant emission sources are added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge for dry goods operations; any wash/sanitization water must meet Panamanian effluent parameters (CONAMA Resolution AD-0034-2002: BOD5 ≤ 200 mg/l, TSS ≤ 220 mg/l). Particle/VOC emissions negligible; dust control via enclosed handling and HEPA filtration. Organic solid waste (spoiled batches, husks) must be segregated and removed by licensed waste haulers to an authorized landfill.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Visto Bueno del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (biennial fire safety certificate) for the warehouse and office; municipal structural load inspection certification for racking and mezzanine areas; emergency evacuation plan approval; and MITRADEL occupational health and safety workplace clearance (Registro de Seguridad Ocupacional) with annual employer health-and-safety compliance certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) – Panama; official portal: dgi.gob.pa and e-Service platform 'SIE' (Sistema de Información Económica) at sie.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from the DGI for any business activity. The foreign owner appoints a resident Foundation Agent who completes Form RUC-1, submits the foundation charter and agent’s ID, and registers with the DGI (and MCI's Aviso de Operación for commercial operation). Non-resident owners do not require a local presence; the foundation may also register as an exporter via the SEM (Sistema Electrónico de Comercio) of the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections exist under Panamanian law. An eligible small taxpayer may opt into the Régimen Simplificado de Tributación (simplified tax regime) for ITBMS; exporters may elect to register under the Export Regime and apply zero-rating. No other statutory entity classification elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – Panama VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0 (mandatory RUC and ITBMS registration for all persons carrying out taxable economic activity in Panama; any threshold is limited to the small-taxpayer simplified regime at annual gross sales ≤ USD 36,000)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates phased electronic invoicing ('factura electrónica') through the DGI’s SIE platform. Registered taxpayers must issue invoices in a digital format containing a unique authentication hash code and QR, and transmit them electronically to the DGI for validation at issuance. Authorized software must integrate via DGI web services/API. Export operations must also be reported through the customs electronic single-window (VUPA).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the effective sale and export of physical goods (e.g., dried goji berries) that leave Panamanian territory to a foreign buyer. The seller must maintain proof that title and risk passed outside Panama. Services are zero-rated only when performed and used entirely offshore. The exporter must hold a valid RUC and be enrolled in the DGI export registry and the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias' export registry.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación — DUA)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to documentary audit by the DGI and customs authorities. Any fraudulent claim to zero-rate an internal sale or misrepresent export documents triggers the application of ITBMS at 7% on the transaction plus interest (1% per month) and fines under Arts. 780–817 of the Código Fiscal; documentary forgery is a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment. The DGI may claw back refunds for up to 3 years after the tax period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no Central Bank and issues no paper currency. Banking and foreign-exchange administration is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under the General Banking Law (Decreto Ley No. 9 de 26 de febrero de 1998). The U.S. Dollar (USD) is unlimited legal tender under the Monetary Regime Law (Ley 84 de 1941); the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) circulates solely as fractional coins issued through Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) at a fixed 1:1 ratio to USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital and current account transactions are fully convertible with no exchange controls, no surrender obligations, and no panamanian-source remittance withholding on PIF distributions. Profit remittance by a Private Interest Foundation (Ley 25 de 1995) to foreign beneficiaries is unrestricted, subject only to documentary proof that income is non-Panamanian-source (territorial tax model). USD settlement of dried goji berry trade, EUR or CNY invoices, and overseas supplier payments is lawful without pre-approval; only reported via FECI/Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) when individual wire movements exceed USD 300,000 equivalent or trigger suspicious-transaction filing under Ley 23 de 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, or prescribed repatriation window for export proceeds. The PA_PIF exporter must, however, channel receipts through SBP-regulated banks or licensed fintech institutions, denominate the Foundation books in USD, retain SBP-compliant MT103 records, and preserve the electronic export declaration plus customs clearance issued by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas for at least five years (Código de Comercio Art. 64).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for licensed domestic entities, LOW for unlicensed offshore EMIs. Under the SBP Fintech framework (Ley 21 de 2017 and SBP e-money regulations), a locally licensed EMI or digital wallet provider (e.g., Wallter, Nexsys, Criptofacil) may open B2B treasury accounts with remote KYC for vendor disbursements under USD 50,000 per wire; however, correspondent USD rails for suppliers are indirect and LC/SWIFT MT103 settlement remains limited to commercial banks. Offshore EMIs without an SBP license may not legally hold Panamanian foundation deposits unless they partner with a Panamanian licensed bank or act as mere payment facilitators.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The PIF's founding council members and the designated signatory must present apostilled originals of the foundation deed, Registro Público certificate of the foundation and council officers, and a certified power of attorney from the resident agent. Banco General and Banistmo generally require one in-person compliance interview at a Panamanian branch or at their international banking unit; no notarial 'double witness' requirement applies beyond the foundation deed. SBP-licensed digital banks permit fully remote video-KYC onboarding for the PA_PIF only when beneficial ownership (Ley 23 de 2015) is conclusively identified and an SBP AML waiver is approved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque PIF structure with nominee Foundation Council and undisclosed reservista/beneficiary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vector of documents: apostilled Ley 25 de 1995 foundation deed, Registro Público certificate of foundation registration showing council composition, beneficial-ownership schedule naming each reservista and council member, sworn economic-substance statement signed by the resident agent, and SBP-compliant FECI initial-client risk classification form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag on dried herbal commodity invoices (quantity/price mismatch, round-tripping)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file: proforma and final commercial invoices, export declaration from the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas, bill of lading, phytosanitary export certificate of the Ministerio de Desarrollo Agropecuario (MIDA), certificate of origin for China/Ningxia suppliers, inspection report, and the applicant's corporate beneficial-owner declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal wire velocity or multiple unrelated originators wiring the PIF capital account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy and cash-flow forecast, subscribed capital contribution agreements per founder, SWIFT MT103 narrative showing payment purpose as 'Founding funds for PIF PA_PIF', OFAC/UN sanctions and PEP screening output for all counterparties, and any UAF suspicious-transaction report voluntarily filed by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency ambiguity and non-declared Panama-source activity of the PIF
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGI annual affidavit (Declaración Jurada de Renta) confirming zero Panama-source income, an updated RUC certificate if the commercial venture triggers inscription, storage and handling evidence limited to bonded warehouse re-export, and an attorney legal-opinion letter confirming the territorial scope of the Foundation under Ley 25 de 1995.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Injection must be wired via SWIFT MT103 exclusively to the Capital Escrow Account opened with an SBP-licensed bank; the remittance must identify 'PA_PIF' exactly as registered in the Registro Público and include a narrative purpose: 'Founding endowment -- PA_PIF -- ISIC 4631 goji berry export'. For injections above USD 300,000 equivalent, the receiving bank files the FECI report to UAF and the founder must attach a source-of-funds certificate (bank statement of the remitter, sale agreement of assets, or loan agreement). Currency may be USD, EUR, or CNY; conversion to USD is executed at the bank's free market rate with a conversion ticket retained for audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for dried goji berries and herbal botanicals clear via (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account advance and deferred payments, (ii) irrevocable commercial letters of credit governed by UCP 600 confirmed by a prime correspondent bank (e.g., HSBC, JP Morgan, or Deutsche Bank routed through the local tier-1 bank), and (iii) documentary collection (D/P and D/A) for low-value repetitive orders. Every disbursement above USD 500,000 requires dual signature authorization and must clear SBP OFAC/UN sanctions filters; the PIF maintains a treasury ledger reconciling each MT103 with the underlying export invoice and customs declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable FX forward with Banco General or Banistmo treasury desks under an ISDA FX Annex
USD/CNH non-deliverable forward (NDF) booked through a licensed international bank, since CNY is not deliverable within Panama
USD/EUR cross-currency swap under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement for hedging long-term goji berry procurement contracts
Natural hedge via offsetting EUR/USD time deposits and forward rate agreements aligned to the quarterly purchasing cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Legal Entity Government Fee - Private Interest Foundation Unified Annual Tax (Tasa Unica Anual) under Law 66 of 2014
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) - Ventanilla Unica electronic payment portal, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar deadline of 31 May each year; no anniversary-based alternative applies to foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest of 10% per annum plus monthly surcharge; Public Registry blocks inscription of notarial instruments and issuance of certificates of good standing; arrears beyond one fiscal year place the foundation in DGI default status and expose it to administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Declaration under Law 52 of 2016 (Declaracion Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) - Electronic Beneficial Ownership Registry platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 April covering the preceding calendar year; intra-year changes to the beneficial ownership schedule must be updated within 30 days of the transfer or modification event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from USD 500 to USD 10,000 per infraction and up to USD 50,000 in aggravated or recurrent cases; Public Registry recording blocks and loss of good standing certification; two consecutive unfiled annual periods may lead to judicial dissolution at DGI request

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Aviso de Operacion Annual Renewal (Commercial Operating Notice under Law 76 of 2009)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipality of Panama - General Directorate of Municipal Revenue; parallel obligations apply in any municipality where physical premises or local commercial activity exist
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Municipal fiscal year renewal due by 31 March without surcharge; absolute payment deadline before 30 June to avoid coercive enforcement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus monthly late interest; after 30 June the municipal treasury initiates administrative foreclosure (apremio), suspension of the operating notice, closure of commercial premises, and potential embargo of bank accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certificate of Good Standing / Certified Copy of Foundation Existence and Representation (Certificado de Personeria Juridica)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Publico de Panama) - General Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On demand; available immediately after the annual government fee is cleared and no registry encumbrances exist; recommend synchronization with each annual banking KYC and Swift TT counterparty review cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not a fixed-date filing; issuance is refused while the annual government fee or registry charges are outstanding, and counterparties and bankers treat the absence of a current certificate as loss of legal standing, freezing payment rails and trade credit lines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foundation Council Annual Meeting Minutes, Economic Substance Record and Statutory Books Retention Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent office / Foundation seat in Panama; private records maintained for inspection by DGI, Public Registry agents and the Foundation Council
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual council meeting and formal minutes prepared within 90 days after the 31 December fiscal year-end or as otherwise fixed by the Foundation Charter; books and underlying records retained for the full 7-year statutory period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine applies to private minutes; however, missing minutes, absent accounting ledgers or incomplete beneficiary registers breach the documentation duties of Law 25 of 1995 and Law 52 of 2016, exposing foundation council members to civil liability and enabling DGI sanctions during tax or AML audits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Law 25 of 1995 imposes no mandatory independent audit on a Private Interest Foundation solely by reason of foundation status; an independent audit by a Panamanian licensed public accountant becomes compulsory when (i) the Foundation Charter or Regulations expressly require it, (ii) a beneficiary or council member exercises the statutory supervisory right, or (iii) annual gross revenue from Panamanian-source commercial activity exceeds USD 3,000,000, at which point the DGI requires audited financial statements under the Corporate Tax Code; below this threshold unaudited compiled financial statements satisfy routine DGI and registered agent compliance
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama's Accounting Directorate for general-purpose reporting; IFRS for SMEs is permissible for non-public and smaller operations; local Panama GAAP remains acceptable for internal foundation recordkeeping where no DGI statutory filing is triggered; the Public Registry does not require annual financial statement filing for Private Interest Foundations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 25 of 1995 and Law 52 of 2016 require the foundation to identify all ultimate beneficial owners, including the founder, foundation council members, protector, beneficiaries, and certificate holders entitled to foundation assets, on a private register maintained at the registered agent's office in Panama; the DGI electronic Beneficial Ownership Registry mirrors this register and requires an annual confirmation declaration by 30 April for the preceding calendar year, with intra-year transfers or redistributions of economic interests updated within 30 days; the Foundation Council resolution approving any beneficiary change must accompany the DGI update, and the registered agent is obligated to flag persistent silence before the statutory deadline
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Officers
Register of Foundation Certificate Holders where certificates are issued
Minute Book of Foundation Council Meetings (Libro de Actas)
Statutory Accounting Books and Supporting Ledgers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to USD 1,200 per annum at standard Panama City corporate agents covering registered office, resident agent, annual government fee processing and Law 52 UBO maintenance; full-service international trust and foundation providers range from USD 1,500 to USD 2,500 per annum
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 5,500 for an annual IFRS compiled-to-audited engagement for a medium-volume dried goji berry and herbal botanical wholesale exporter; bookkeeping-only and unaudited tax preparation services range from USD 1,000 to USD 2,000 where the USD 3,000,000 compulsory audit threshold is not reached

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial tax system. Only Panama-source income is within the scope of the 25% corporate income tax. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in the international bulk export of organic dried Lycium and herbal botanicals can achieve an effective Panamanian tax rate of 0% if the export sales, contract conclusion, delivery, and title transfer occur outside Panamanian territory and all supporting commercial evidence is properly documented. Preferential regimes (e.g., Multinational Headquarters SEM, Panama Pacifico, E-Empresa) may further reduce Panamanian-source tax to 0%–5% for licensed re-export or logistics activities, but a standard PIF does not automatically access them.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 750 (Declaración Jurada de Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI online portal (DGI en Línea / Sistema de Recaudación Virtual) at www.dgi.gob.pa; digital or certified-subscription filing is required for taxpayers with annual gross income above B/.3,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 750) plus quarterly advance income tax payments (Form 720-A) submitted in April, July, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the PIF's fiscal year. For a calendar-year PIF, the return is due on or before 31 March of the following year; for an authorized special fiscal year, the due date is the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end. The DGI may publish a staggered annual filing schedule based on the RUC ending digit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross gross revenue from all Panamanian-source sales and services before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue with an economic nexus in Panama (e.g., local delivery, storage, or order management). Foreign-title-transfer export sales of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals should be excluded and supported by contracts, bills of lading, and independent payment flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from foreign-source activities, outside the Panamanian territorial tax net.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a written reconciliation and documentary proof that the commercial activity, contract conclusion, and economic substance occurred outside Panama. Do not net foreign losses against Panamanian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, including purchase cost of dried Lycium, herbal botanicals, packaging, freight, customs duties, and direct export logistics.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate COGS to Panamanian-source sales only where inventory is physically imported into or consumed within Panama; foreign-sourced inventory costs should be excluded from the taxable pool.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible Panamanian operating expenses such as commissions, port storage, freight, licence fees, and banking charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred through the Panamanian PIF and evidenced by DGI-validated electronic invoices and actual wire-transfer payments; retain allocation memoranda showing foreign overhead allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductible expenses and executed loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a properly documented non-resident PIF with exclusively foreign-source trading income, report 0.00; complete and file a defensive zero return to preserve audit protection and avoid reactivation of the statute of limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed income tax at the 25% statutory rate on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign-source income is the only revenue, the computed tax is zero. Where Panamanian-source profit exists, apply 25%, then credit quarterly advance payments previously remitted on Form 720-A.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers: (1) a surcharge of 10% of the tax due where the return is submitted within one month after the deadline, rising to 20% thereafter; (2) monthly interest at 1.5% on the unpaid tax; (3) administrative fines of B/.100 to B/.10,000 where no tax liability is shown; (4) suspension of the RUC, denial of the DGI's certificate of good standing, and exclusion from government and banking contracting; and (5) in persistent cases, official estimated assessment and coercive tax collection through bank embargo and asset liens.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on distributions made out of profits already subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; 10% on distributions made out of Panamanian-source profits that have not borne the general corporate tax (provided they are not properly documented foreign-source income, which remains outside the tax net under the territorial system).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder seeking DTA relief must submit a formal written request to the DGI before or at the time of distribution, attaching: (1) a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country revenue authority; (2) a beneficial ownership and legal-residence declaration; (3) financial statements and tax records showing the distributable profits have been subject to Panamanian tax; and (4) the applicable treaty article. The DGI may issue a provisional or final ruling; the payer is not allowed to reduce withholding until the relief is admitted. Panama's narrow DTA network includes, among others, Korea, Mexico, Portugal, Singapore, and Spain; treaty benefits frequently require analysis of the PIF's transparency and beneficial-owner status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest sourced in Panama and paid to a non-resident is generally subject to statutory withholding at 8%. Royalty payments sourced in Panama for patents, trademarks, copyrights, know-how, and similar intangible property are subject to statutory withholding at 12.5%. Under certain DTAs, interest may be reduced to 5% and royalties to 10%, subject to the successful completion of the treaty-relief protocol and clear documentation of beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.3,000,000 in annual consolidated gross income; mandatory Master File and Local File (Transfer Pricing Report) are required above this threshold. A Local File may also be demanded where the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds B/.1,000,000, and a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for multinational groups with annual consolidated revenue equivalent to or above B/.850,000,000.
